sections.title: A language is a way of doing something
sections.content: Hungarian says *in* a language with an ending on the language word: *-ul* or *-ül*. You add it to the word for the language: *Beszélek magyarul.* (I speak Hungarian.) Back vowels (a, o, u) take *-ul*: *magyar → magyarul*, *angol → angolul*, *spanyol → spanyolul*, *olasz → olaszul*. Front vowels (e, é, ö, ü) take *-ül*: *német → németül*. *Francia* ends in the back vowel *a*, so it takes *-ul*: *franciául*. You already know this back-or-front choice from *-ban/-ben*.

sections.title: No -t, and no capital letters
sections.content: The language word does not take the accusative *-t*: say *Olvasok angolul*, not *Olvasok angolt*. Names of languages are written with a small letter. The language word can stand before the verb or after it: *Beszélek spanyolul. Spanyolul beszélek.*
The ending is not optional. *Beszélek magyar* is wrong; Hungarian needs *magyarul*. Choose the vowel by the last vowel of the language word: *németül*, but *angolul*.
